thread:
nora: dropping a follow-up from the architecture sync. we kept circling on cross-shard fairness vs. single-shard isolation. wanted to sketch a different angle: virtual shards + credit morphing.

ben: fancy name. can you unpack "virtual shard"? how's that different from tenant->shard mapping?

nora: sure. physical shards still exist, but each shard hosts multiple "virtual pools" mapped to tenant cohorts. virtual pools are lightweight namespaces for fairness and policy, and can be remapped across physical hosts without moving tenant state.

ali: so migration is remap of vpool -> physical_shard, not moving counters. that could be cheaper. what's credit morphing?

nora: credit morphing = a small runtime that can reinterpret a virtual pool's credits across quota dimensions. e.g., convert 1 embedding-unit = 0.4 text-tokens for that tenant based on historical cost. lets us enforce composite quotas locally without global checks.

sam: interesting. that helps multi-dimensional quotas. but how do we avoid violations when morph factors are stale?

nora: local shards keep morph parameters with ttl. conservative defaults on expiry. if stale and usage risky, fall into slow-path consult. also we can estimate risk by tracking divergence between predicted vs actual cost and circuit-break when error > threshold.

ben: coordination: how do we decide to remap a vpool? we need signals for donor/recipient capacity without heavy chatter.

ali: propose a pull model: physical shards publish tiny health ticks with three numbers: CPU_load, free_credit_pct, recent_spill_rate. pack into 32 bytes and broadcast via pubsub every 300-700ms. remapper pulls ticks and computes candidate remaps.

sam: keep ticks non-tenant-specific to avoid leaks. good. what about short bursts — do we migrate vpool mid-burst? migration cost should be minimal since counters are virtual pointers.

nora: yes. remap is atomic pointer swap in control-plane metadata: vpool.owner := new_shard. we log generation id so data-plane rejects older tokens. if migration fails, we roll back pointer and emit metrics.

ben: anti-duplication / contention? two remappers might race. need compare-and-swap on owner generation.

nora: exactly: CAS on owner record. loser backoff. no per-request consensus.

ali: what about abuse scoring? if tenant spans models and vpools, how do we arrive at consistent reputation?

sam: central reputation service with event-streams. shards append summarized events (score deltas) and pull aggregated reputation snapshot with 1s TTL. For urgent bans we use a push notify channel.

ben: latency concerns: morphing + local checks must be sub-ms. slow-path consult should be <5ms added but rare. what's our target for local-only pass rate?

nora: aim: 99.92% local-only. slow-path <0.08%. that matches other infra SLOs. we'll validate in canary.

ali: security: remap ops and virtual pool metadata must be signed and namespaced by org + region. pubsub ticks are authenticated and only include shard-id and aggregates.

sam: neat idea: token vending machine for cross-vpool spill. donor shard can mint a short-lived voucher (signed) that a recipient shard redeems. voucher contains vpool_id, amount, expiry, and donor_gen. recipient validates donor_gen matches owner snapshot to avoid stale vouchers.

nora: vouchers work well with virtual pools because vouchers reference vpool id, not tenant counters. if vpool remaps, donor_gen mismatch makes vouchers invalid.

ben: observability: dashboards need vpool -> shard mapping over time, voucher issuance/consumption, morph error rate, remap churn. plus synthetic canary that pushes a vpool to saturation.

ali: rollout plan: 1) implement vpool metadata + CAS remap in control-plane. 2) enable ticks + remapper read-only to surface suggestions. 3) voucher prototype + morphing library on a small canary subset (5% tenants). 4) enable active remap for low-risk vpools.

sam: testing: traffic-replay for 72h, chaos tests where shards drop mid-remap, and a cost-model check for morphing calibration.

nora: ops-playbook: auto-disable remapper if remap/sec > threshold or if voucher-redeem failures spike. provide quick flag to pin vpool to current shard.

ben: any concerns about billing / legal caps? morphing can't relax MUST_FAIL quotas. those remain enforced via slow-path strong-check. morph only affects BEST_EFFORT heuristics.

ali: also add a conservative safety: if morph error grows beyond X% for a vpool, mark it MUST_FAIL until manual review.

sam: ops-bot: can you open a follow-up ticket with the rollout steps + dashboards + simulation tasks? :robot_face:

ops-bot: created INFRA-2005 "virtual-pools + credit-morphing prototype & rollout" and linked this thread.

nora: assigning myself for prototyping vpool remap. ali will take morph model calibration. ben will own voucher prototype. sam will own observability + runbooks.

ben: love it 680 let's validate with canary in two sprints.

ali: i'll start a doc for morph tuning and examples.

sam: i'll sketch the dashboard layout and alerts.

nora: thanks all, closing this thread. we'll post the RFC addendum with diagrams. :seedling:
